title: Wipro and Databricks Launch Dedicated AI Practice to Scale Enterprise Data Transformation
excerpt: The Indian IT giant establishes a self-contained Databricks business practice to help enterprises move from isolated AI pilots to production-ready deployments across banking, healthcare, telecom, and energy.
body:
• Wipro has launched a dedicated Databricks business practice to build industry-specific AI solutions, integrating capabilities in agentic AI, data modernization, and analytics
  • The practice builds on more than 300 agentic AI and data use cases already delivered across banking, healthcare, telecom, manufacturing, and energy
  • Databricks recognized the partnership with its 2025 Banking Partner of the Year and 2026 Innovation Partner of the Year awards
  • The collaboration integrates Wipro Intelligence™, the WEGA agent-native delivery platform, and Databricks Genie for natural-language data interaction

From Pilot to Production

Wipro Limited announced on July 27 an enhanced partnership with Databricks to help enterprises modernize their data foundations and accelerate AI adoption at scale. The centerpiece of the deal is a new, self-contained Databricks business practice within Wipro — a dedicated unit designed to drive industry-specific AI solutions rather than the fragmented, one-off pilot projects that have characterized much of enterprise AI deployment.

https://x.com/_Investor_Feed_/status/2081685122114543941

The announcement, made via Business Wire, signals a shift in how large IT services firms are organizing around the AI opportunity: not as a horizontal capability bolted onto existing consulting, but as a distinct business unit with its own team of platform specialists, consulting experts, and industry verticalists.

"Our long-standing collaboration with Databricks reflects a shared commitment to help enterprises move from AI experimentation to measurable value."

— Kanwar Singh, Managing Partner – Technology Services, Wipro Limited

What the Practice Will Do

The new business practice integrates Databricks' capabilities in agentic AI, data modernization, application development, and analytics with Wipro Intelligence™, the company's suite of AI-powered platforms and solutions. It will also leverage WEGA, Wipro's agent-native delivery platform, to help enterprises transition from legacy systems to scalable, AI-ready data architectures.

A key tool in the arsenal is Databricks Genie, an AI-powered assistant that enables both business and technical users to interact with enterprise data using natural language. The practice aims to help business users see value faster by lowering the technical barrier to data exploration and insight generation.

Across industries, the practice will build context-aware solutions targeting core business challenges: end-to-end wealth management and portfolio optimization in banking; planning resiliency for manufacturing amid macroeconomic volatility; agentic AI-led sales transformation for telecoms; and asset visibility and performance improvement for energy and large-asset industries.

Track Record and Recognition

The practice is not starting from scratch. Wipro has delivered more than 300 agentic AI and data use cases across industries, according to the company. That experience has translated into concrete results — a 40% reduction in total cost of ownership for an energy major's modernization program, and a 50% boost in request-for-quote productivity for a large retailer.

Databricks has recognized the partnership with its 2025 Banking Partner of the Year Award and the 2026 Innovation Partner of the Year Award, according to the joint announcement. Wipro holds the status of Global Elite Databricks partner, with more than 1,500 engineers and consultants dedicated to the partnership.

"This global practice with Wipro will enable enterprises to build trusted data foundations and deploy production-ready AI at scale, turning data intelligence into real, measurable business impact."

— Kori O'Brien, Senior Vice President, Partnerships, Databricks

The Indian IT Angle

For Wipro (NYSE: WIT), the partnership deepens its positioning as an AI-first services company at a time when Indian IT firms are competing aggressively for enterprise AI budgets. The company, which employs over 240,000 people across 65 countries, has been investing heavily in its AI capabilities as clients demand more than traditional outsourcing.

The Databricks partnership also feeds into a broader trend among Indian IT services companies — including TCS, Infosys, and HCL Tech — of establishing dedicated practices around major platform vendors to capture enterprise AI spending. The difference, Wipro argues, is the depth of industry-specific solutions rather than generic platform implementation.

What to Watch

The test for the new practice will be whether it can deliver on the promise of scaling AI beyond isolated use cases. Enterprises have spent years running AI proofs of concept without achieving production-grade deployment. Wipro and Databricks are betting that a dedicated practice — with its own P&L incentives and specialized teams — can break that pattern. The partnership is expected to expand through joint go-to-market efforts and co-created solutions tailored to specific industry verticals.
